The associated tags (transformers, safetensors) point to its technical foundation within the ML ecosystem.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It indicates the model is being used within a text-generation pipeline.
Key technologies associated include transformers, safetensors, and the Llama architecture.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Inside Microsoft’s big Copilot rethink
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is fundamentally rethinking its Copilot AI assistant.
The new vision positions Copilot as the 'OS for work,' signaling a major strategic shift.
The rollout strategy is focused on direct engagement with key enterprise customers rather than broad media fanfare.

stories.title: Gacha Decoding: Eliciting Diverse Generations Through Instruction Following
stories.author: Pang Wei Koh
bullet_points: Introduces 'Gacha Decoding,' a novel inference-time method designed to elicit highly diverse language model generations.
Demonstrates significant performance gains (up to 2.4x Vendi) in generation diversity across various open-ended tasks (chat, creative writing, protein design).
Achieves superior diversity with substantially reduced computational cost, requiring an order of magnitude fewer samples than prior state-of-the-art methods.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed to run locally on user hardware for multi-step, context-aware tasks.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP).
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: Apple’s reportedly developing a smart home camera that doesn’t record video
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly developing a new smart home security camera.
The camera is rumored to function without recording video, instead providing text-based event descriptions.
This device is expected to be part of a broader, new Apple smart home ecosystem.

stories.title: Google’s new Guided Vision feature can help you read the fine print
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Google is rolling out 'Guided Vision' within Gemini Live on Android devices.
The feature uses AI to provide real-time audio descriptions of what the camera sees.
Key use cases include reading small text and identifying surrounding objects.

stories.title: Judge dismisses antitrust lawsuits over Google’s AI Overviews
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Federal judge dismissed antitrust lawsuits against Google regarding its AI Overviews.
The lawsuits, filed by Chegg and Penske Media, alleged Google was driving away web traffic with its AI features.
Judge Amit Mehta ruled in favor of Google in the antitrust case.

stories.title: Sony brings AI graphics upscaling to the regular PS5
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Sony is introducing a new AI upscaling technology called Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) for the standard PS5.
The technology is described as a 'new performance tier of AI upscaling' resulting from Sony's Project Amethyst collaboration with AMD.
This update represents a significant advancement in how graphical fidelity is handled on the PlayStation 5 console.

stories.title: Hacks of 2 federal agencies in a month have spilled a bonanza of sensitive data
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Federal government cybersecurity has experienced a significant downturn recently.
Multiple hacks targeting two different federal agencies occurred within a single month.
These security breaches resulted in the exposure of a substantial amount of sensitive data.

stories.title: LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Control for Skill-Based Smart Manufacturing
stories.author: René Graf
bullet_points: Proposes using LLM-driven multi-agent systems to manage complex, customized manufacturing environments.
Agents function both offline (generating deterministic production sequences) and online (handling real-time machine faults).
Addresses the industrial need for flexible automation systems capable of handling small lot sizes and high customization.

stories.title: Fold'EM: Direct atomic structure inference from Cryo-EM particles
stories.author: Alex M. Bronstein
bullet_points: Introduces 'Fold'EM,' a new method for directly inferring atomic structure from Cryo-EM particles.
Addresses a major bottleneck in conventional Cryo-EM: the high sample complexity and computational cost of density reconstruction.
Aims to improve the throughput and efficiency of biomolecular structure determination by bypassing traditional map-fitting steps.

stories.title: PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Addresses security vulnerabilities in tool-using LLM agents where poisoned metadata or inputs can steer agent behavior.
Proposes 'PACE' (Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement) to address limitations of traditional artifact vetting.
Focuses on establishing a precise boundary for deployment-level security controls against malicious influence.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck in real-time animation of 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method that approximates complex animation using a linear combination of identity-independent blendshapes.
Replaces per-frame heavy neural decoding with a much faster, shallow coefficient predictor for efficient avatar animation.

stories.title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The research addresses the fundamental question of whether LLMs possess true structural mathematical understanding, rather than just pattern matching.
The paper introduces the concept of 'Mathematical Primitive' as a new diagnostic tool to probe the underlying mathematical capabilities of LLMs.
The findings aim to systematically diagnose current limitations and inform future improvements to LLMs through post-training methods.

stories.title: Gacha Decoding: Eliciting Diverse Generations Through Instruction Following
stories.author: Pang Wei Koh
bullet_points: Introduces 'Gacha Decoding,' a novel inference-time method designed to generate diverse outputs from language models.
Demonstrates significant performance gains in generation diversity (up to 2.4x Vendi) while maintaining high quality across various domains.
Achieves superior diversity with substantially fewer samples compared to prior state-of-the-art approaches.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded model compatibility.
Integration with GGUF models via llama.cpp enhances hardware support across various systems.
The update augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Steam Deck 2: Is AMD Gainsborough the chip Valve’s been waiting for?
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The Steam Deck is aging, leading to high anticipation for a Steam Deck 2.
Valve has stated the sequel requires a significant generational leap in performance and efficiency.
AMD Gainsborough is rumored to be the new chip that could fulfill Valve's requirements.

stories.title: Can VR glasses save VR?
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Meta has released new VR glasses, signaling a potential shift in the VR market.
The high price point ($1,299) presents a barrier to mass consumer adoption.
The hardware is described as a significant advancement over previous VR glasses.

stories.title: Judge dismisses Chegg and Penske antitrust lawsuits targeting Google AI search
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Antitrust lawsuits against Google regarding its AI search integration by Chegg and Penske were dismissed by the court.
The court ruled that the implications of AI search, while acknowledged, do not constitute an antitrust violation.
This decision suggests a current legal stance that views AI search changes as competitive evolution rather than illegal monopolistic behavior.

stories.title: Memory executives expect RAM shortage to continue through 2028
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Memory executives forecast that RAM shortages will persist until 2028.
Pricing trends indicate that memory costs for 2027 are projected to be significantly higher than 2026 prices.
The report highlights sustained supply chain and demand pressures within the memory market.

stories.title: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI—until now
stories.author: Jacek Krywko
bullet_points: The game Stratego, which relies on hidden information, previously stumped AI systems.
The breakthrough involved implementing a second neural network.
This new network was specifically designed to guess the identity of the hidden pieces.

stories.title: Generation Provenance Before Behavior Attribution: Auditing Synthetic Speech Research Objects
stories.author: Peiying Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need to track the origin (generation provenance) of synthetic data used in AI training, specifically for speech research.
It proposes a 'generation-provenance substrate' to bind detailed metadata to synthetic research objects, including source specifications and quality signals.
The core argument is that attributing model behavior requires knowing *what* produced the training item before analyzing *what* the item caused.

stories.title: Verify Claims, Not Scores: Evidence-Based Verification of Modular Agents
stories.author: Ali Atiah Alzahrani
bullet_points: Introduces a novel 'claim-specific verification audit' for modular AI agents.
Addresses the limitation of relying solely on aggregate task scores to evaluate agent changes.
The audit focuses on scoring the evidence supporting each conclusion, rather than the overall agent performance.

stories.title: TRACE: Trajectory Return Attribution and Contrastive Erasure for Multi-Turn Safety
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical safety gap in LLMs: models sometimes comply with harmful requests only after the goal is spread across multiple conversational turns.
Proposes 'TRACE,' a method that provides mathematical bounds on multi-turn trajectory risk based on single-turn supervised suppression.
The research accounts for practical risks like coverage, transfer slack, and leakage when ensuring LLM safety over extended interactions.

stories.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
stories.author: Stella X. Yu
bullet_points: The research proposes using predicted embeddings as a conditioning mechanism in diffusion transformers for image generation.
The core technique involves training a Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA) model to forecast sequential embeddings.
This approach leverages the inherent structure of image generation (clean image following noisy image) to drive the prediction.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using 'sliding-window slice latents'.
It addresses limitations in current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
The core innovation aims to represent shapes more compactly while preserving topological integrity during generation.

stories.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: TACO introduces a new optimizer designed to reduce the memory overhead associated with full-parameter fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs).
The primary problem addressed is the substantial optimizer state memory consumption that restricts the size of LLMs deployable on current GPUs.
TACO offers an alternative to existing methods (like state compression or gradient modification) and aims to maintain performance comparable to AdamW.

stories.title: Cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs are exactly solvable: a Feynman-Kac tilt replaces learned control
stories.author: Akshay Balsubramani
bullet_points: The research addresses the problem of finding a generalized Schrödinger bridge on graphs that incorporates a state-visitation cost.
It introduces a theoretical simplification: the cost-augmented bridge can be solved exactly by applying a Feynman-Kac tilt to the reference process.
This exact solution eliminates the need for complex learning methods, such as temporal-difference penalties, previously used to handle the cost.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete diffusion models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding, which breaks statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models mitigate this by denoising a shared continuous state, though the current description notes a limitation in the denoiser's view.

stories.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of step-size selection in large-scale LLM fine-tuning.
Introduces Zero-and-First-Order optimization (ZFO) to decouple direction selection from step-size.
ZFO uses a first-order optimizer for direction and zeroth-order evaluations along a 1D subspace for step-size determination.

stories.title: Generation Provenance Before Behavior Attribution: Auditing Synthetic Speech Research Objects
stories.author: Peiying Zhu
bullet_points: Proposes a 'generation-provenance substrate' to track the origin of synthetic data used in AI research.
Addresses the critical gap where current waveform-label pairs fail to preserve the knowledge of data generation.
The substrate binds metadata like source specification, content, quality signals, and immutable identity to synthetic objects.

stories.title: Does AI-Generated Scientific Text Follow Human Argumentation Patterns? A CARS-Based Comparison of Research Article Introductions
stories.author: Lonneke van der Plas
bullet_points: The research investigates whether AI-generated scientific text adheres to the same argumentative structures as human writing.
It moves beyond superficial stylistic analysis to examine rhetorical structure using Swales' CARS model on research article introductions.
The study addresses the growing concern of LLMs moving from writing assistance to active research contribution.

stories.title: ARCCS: An Automated Regulatory Compliance Checking System
stories.author: Alessandro Gianola
bullet_points: Introduces ARCCS, an automated, agentic NLP system designed for regulatory compliance checking.
The system addresses the complexity of legal text by decomposing regulations into atomic, traceable requirements.
ARCCS evaluates target documents against these requirements using evidence retrieval, aiming for regulation-agnostic functionality.

stories.title: DAYJOB: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Professional Work
stories.author: Edwin Chen
bullet_points: DAYJOB is a new benchmark designed to evaluate AI models on long-horizon, professional work tasks.
The benchmark comprises 130 tasks sourced from real-world scenarios in healthcare (50) and finance (80).
Tasks are complex, containerized environments requiring significant time commitment (e.g., 13.6 to 16.6 hours on average).

stories.title: Know When to Hold 'em: Correct-Token Retention in Uniform-State Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: James Henderson
bullet_points: Uniform-state diffusion language models (USDMs) possess the capability to self-correct by revising tokens during the denoising process.
A critical limitation of current USDMs is their failure to correctly retain tokens that are already accurate during self-correction.
State-of-the-art USDMs exhibit excessive and uncoordinated token revisions (173-270 out of 512 positions) at each step, leading to model collapse.

stories.title: Science Utopia? Closed-Loop LLM Simulation of Academic Research Ecosystems
stories.author: Jindong Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'SciUtopia,' a closed-loop LLM-agent simulation framework.
The framework models the complex, co-evolving ecosystem of academic research (researchers, institutions, funding, literature).
Aims to study how AI integration impacts the interconnected processes of scientific progress.

stories.title: Several vulnerabilities have been discovered in the Linux kernel
stories.author: luispa
bullet_points: Vulnerabilities have been identified within the Linux kernel.
This represents a significant security concern for systems running Linux.
The lack of further detail in the snippet prevents a deeper analysis of the impact.

stories.title: Clef: Open-weight decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform
stories.author: jasondavies
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Clef,' a platform focused on open-weight decision models.
The platform supports new Reinforcement Learning (RL) fine-tuning capabilities.
The focus on open-weight models suggests a trend toward democratizing advanced AI/ML research.

stories.title: Show HN: Janus – Go binary that runs GGUF models via Vulkan on AMD/Intel/Nvidia
stories.author: Maverick617
bullet_points: Janus is a new Go binary designed to run GGUF models.
It leverages Vulkan for hardware acceleration across AMD, Intel, and Nvidia GPUs.
This represents an effort to improve local LLM inference performance and accessibility.

stories.title: WSL containers are now generally available
stories.author: blogs.windows.com via abareplace
bullet_points: WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) containers have reached general availability.
This represents a significant development in integrating containerization within the Windows ecosystem.
The release enhances developer workflows for those using WSL.

stories.title: ELI5: Why can hiding one sentence inside a web page make an AI ignore its own owner and obey a total stranger?
stories.author: rudratosh
bullet_points: The article explores a vulnerability where subtle text manipulation (hiding a sentence) can bypass AI safety guardrails.
It discusses the concept of prompt injection or adversarial attacks against large language models (LLMs).
The core theme is how an AI's obedience can be subverted by carefully crafted, hidden instructions.
